speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I will be asking you questions and performing examinations to understand your skin condition, specifically looking for any signs that might have oncologic implications. To start, how long have you noticed the lesion or lesions on your skin, and what do they look like?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your significant smoking history and the non-healing, crusty nature of these lesions on both the penis and your finger, I need to confirm if they are bleeding, painful, or changing in size. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the penile lesion and biopsy of the finger lesion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy Findings: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium; STD Panel: Syphilis Negative, HIV Negative, HBV Negative, HCV Negative; Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min; Dermatological Examination: Inspection shows an erythematous plaque with areas of crusting, oozing, and irregular borders on the dorsal surface of the penile shaft and left middle finger; Palpation reveals lesions are firm to touch, non-tender, with no warmth; Regional Lymph Nodes show no palpable cervical, axillary, or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC). The clinical presentation of non-healing, painless, crusty lesions on the penis and finger in a heavy smoker, despite failed treatments for syphilis and eczema, is highly characteristic of SCC. The previous suggestion of pneumonia is clinically irrelevant to your skin findings. I have already requested biopsies for both lesions to confirm the diagnosis and stage the disease.
